idiom_name: case class Envelope[A](headers, payload) + derived codecs
implementation_notes: Scala reduces the envelope to a case class with a derived codec: case class Envelope[A](headers: Map[String, String], payload: A) plus derivation (Scala 3 derives with Mirror-based type-class derivation, or circe/zio-json derivation on Scala 2) replaces the classic wrapper, and the compiler generates the serializer from the case-class shape. Domain code reads env.payload; metadata lives in the headers map or in transport headers (Pekko/Akka Kafka ConsumerRecord.headers). Write the codec by hand only when the wire format must match an existing non-Scala peer exactly.
pitfalls: Derivation needs codec evidence for every type parameter: a missing Encoder/Decoder shows up as a compile error deep inside the derivation macro, which is easy to misread.
Map-based headers lose ordering and duplicate keys; security-relevant fields must be validated explicitly instead of merely read.
Scala 2 and Scala 3 derivation differ: derives/Mirror-based derivation is Scala 3, while shared code on Scala 2 needs a library derivation such as circe semiauto.
